title: MDlearn Studio · choose the visual world
question: Within your Scientific notebook direction, the roll assigned the Lecture-notes Volume. Keep it, take the alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: The Lecture-notes Volume
options.lineage: physics lecture-note volumes (the red, green and blue books)
options.thesis: Every folder is a numbered volume, every document a chapter, and the wide margin is where you and the AI write back.
options.viewport: Chapter opener: a large chapter numeral in the volume colour, the title, the numbered section list (4–1 … 4–6); spines of your volumes on the left shelf; the margin column on the right holds notes and AI answers aligned to their paragraph.
options.risk: Textbook grammar can drift into the cream-and-italic academic default; kept off by bright paper and saturated volume colour.

raised.raise: Numbers are the headlines: chapter, section and equation numbers are the primary navigation and identity, not decoration.
State is a mark, not a hue: studied tick, shaky half-mark, a flag where you stopped reading, a struck corner for a broken widget.
The library rail is a hairline-ruled dense index with tabular counts, not airy cards.
All study data in tabular numerals in one disciplined mono, aligned in columns.

options.label: The Mission Technical Note
options.lineage: space-mission technical notes and document control
options.thesis: Every document is an issued technical note: document number, issue and revision, numbered requirements, change bars where the AI edited.
options.viewport: A document control block (Doc No., Issue/Rev, Date, Lessons) heads the page; sections carry requirement-style tags; red change bars mark AI edits in the margin.
options.risk: Also the closest to what a space-engineering student already reads at work; can feel bureaucratic, and must never imitate a real agency's branding.

options.label: Factory records catalog
options.thesis: Every artifact is a catalog entry identified only by its number.
options.viewport: A black field with one plot and a catalog number.
options.case: Fuses poorly: a learner needs titles and prose, not codes to decode.

options.label: Cutting-bench select rail
options.thesis: Progress as a perforated rail of frames with marks where you stopped.
options.viewport: A rail of frames across an orange field.
options.case: Fuses partly on study state, loses on reading comfort and audience.
options.kept: State as marks, never hue alone.

options.label: Japanese high-density web
options.thesis: Pack the library into ruled modules.
options.case: Wins density for the library, loses calm reading.
options.kept: Hairline-ruled dense index for the library rail.

options.label: Datamatics field
options.thesis: The data itself as the image.
options.case: Fuses poorly with prose and notes.
options.kept: Tabular mono numerals for all data.

canonCard.label: The notes-app standard
canonCard.thesis: The familiar knowledge-base app: file tree, centred page, side panel.
canonCard.viewport: Sidebar tree, centred Markdown page, collapsible right panel for AI.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from every notes app by design.
